query: Bank X just signed the SOW. They've been running Teradata for 15 years, license expires in June next year, and they want to move to Databricks on Azure. I'm the tech lead and I also own requirements because we have no BA. Kickoff is next week — what should I prepare and what should I ask them first?
My boss dropped a folder of ~200 .sql stored procedure files and 30 SSIS packages from a retail client on me and said 'work out how long it takes to migrate this to Databricks'. Where do I start?

We've been asked to consolidate 7 Databricks workspaces after the merger with Acme — nobody knows who owns half of them and finance says the bill doubled. I need to write up a current-state assessment for the steering committee by end of month. Where do I even start and what data should I pull?

The client says they want a 'modern data platform with AI', but when I dug in they have nothing except a few accounting spreadsheets and one CRM. I need to scope this down to something deliverable in 3 months, and I need to know what to ask them to lock it down.

I have transcripts of 3 interviews with the client's DBA and head of accounting, plus a spec from 2017. Help me pull out the real requirements and flag where the docs and the people contradict each other.

Databricks bill went from 40k to 95k/month in 6 months, CFO wants to know why and what to cut. I have system tables access. How do I approach this assessment properly instead of just eyeballing the usage dashboard?
The client is demanding a real-time revenue dashboard. My team thinks they don't need it but we can't argue it on any solid basis. We're still in discovery, nothing has been built yet.

Write me the assessment report for a SQL Server -> Databricks migration. I already have the table inventory, the list of business rules extracted from the stored procedures, and a list of questions nobody has answered. It's for the CTO to decide wave 1 scope.

The DBA who built our entire DW is retiring in March. Before he goes I need to capture what the 87 stored procedures actually do and what's not in any spec. We're going to Databricks eventually but right now it's about not losing the knowledge

A partner wants us to share transaction data with them over Delta Sharing and legal is nervous. I need to assess what we can share, at what grain, and who I need to ask before I promise the partner anything.
Write me a DLT pipeline that loads the customer table from bronze to silver with SCD type 2 using AUTO CDC, source is Auto Loader reading parquet from ADLS.
My nightly job runs 5 hours on an 8-node cluster, mostly one MERGE into a 2-billion-row table. Tune it for me — how should I partition, liquid clustering or z-order?
Set up a Databricks asset bundle for this repo to deploy jobs via GitHub Actions, 3 targets dev/staging/prod, running as a service principal.
Write the Unity Catalog grant statements for the analyst team: SELECT only on the gold schema, no visibility into bronze or silver, mask the email column.
Write user stories and acceptance criteria for the customer onboarding screens in our mobile app — KYC upload, OTP verification, consent checkbox. Need them in Jira format.
My DLT pipeline throws 'duplicate key in APPLY CHANGES INTO' on the customer table during a full refresh; the source uses updated_at as sequence_by. Help me debug it.
Compare Databricks vs Snowflake vs Fabric cost for a ~5TB/day workload. I need a table to drop into a slide so my boss can pick a vendor.
Write SQL over gold.fact_sales for revenue by month by region for the last 12 months with year-over-year comparison, for this week's report.
Make a 15-slide deck for the leadership team on the 2027 digital transformation roadmap. There's a data platform section but it's mostly a high-level overview.
our Databricks pipeline finished migrating last quarter; now I need to set up Lakehouse Monitoring / data quality monitoring on the gold tables and alerting to Slack when drift is detected
